selected.name: Formal claims quantified, with the conditions they hold under
selected.instruction: Score the precision of any theoretical statement. 10: rates, sizes or complexities are given explicitly along with the setting they hold in, so a reader could in principle contradict them (coreset of size O(m + poly(k/eps)) constructible in near-linear time; at most O~(d^2 H^5 / eps^2) trajectories within H deployments under a linear MDP with feature dimension d; complexity reduced from O(C^2 L^5) to O(C L^3 log L) while remaining strictly equivariant). 5: a named theorem or property with partial conditions. 0: theory vocabulary with no content the reader can restate: 'we give theoretical proof that our method is stable and non-dissipative', 'produces lower-variance gradient estimates', with no assumptions, no rate, no comparison point. Score 0 also when there is no formal claim.
selected.rationale: Precise-theory abstracts are the most extreme dense-high / card-low cases in the slice (R45, R57, R38, R24): they carry no benchmark table, no ablation and often no code, so a criterion bank organized around empirical hygiene has nothing to credit, while the quantified statement is the whole contribution. R60 and R31 assert properties in the same register without quantification, and are the mirror direction.
member_names: Decisive, unhedged claim paired with breadth of claimed regime
Formal claims quantified, with the conditions they hold under
Formal precision of claims vs vague superlatives
Generality claim paired with explicit non-requirements
Mechanistic account of why the method works, not just that it works
Mechanistic explanation connecting method to underlying phenomena

selected.name: Cross-setting generality
selected.instruction: Score 10 when one coherent formulation is applied across substantially varied tasks or domains with a shared rationale; score 0 when generality is merely claimed or unsupported by textual scope.
selected.rationale: R22 spans graph-level and molecular settings, while R40 describes a common encoding-learning approach across architectures, datasets, and tasks.
member_names: Unification that generates new methods or bounds
Unified Generalization of Prior Disparate Approaches

selected.name: Sharp identification of fundamental flaws in established methods
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the abstract identifies a specific, non-obvious, conceptual failure mode in a widely-used method—the flaw must be structural or mathematical, not merely 'slightly worse performance.' Score 0 if no flaws in existing methods are identified or only vague limitations are mentioned.
selected.rationale: R18 shows that LOLA agents can exhibit 'arrogant' behavior 'directly at odds with convergence,' identifying a structural instability in a celebrated method. R31 reveals that storing models in class-incremental learning 'do[es] not consistently work' once memory budgets are fairly counted, exposing a systemic evaluation flaw. R42 shows current state-of-the-art black-box attacks are 'optimal in a natural sense' yet still improvable, a subtle conceptual gap.
member_names: Novel conceptual reframing changing solution approach
Novelty of the question/problem framing itself
Sharp identification of fundamental flaws in established methods

selected.name: Boundary-Regime Characterization
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the abstract analyzes limiting cases, counterexamples, failure conditions, or regime changes and explains their consequences; score 0 when it discusses only typical operating conditions.
selected.rationale: R10, R12, R43, and R49 emphasize interpolation thresholds, nonconvergence examples, function-class dependence, or unstable variance estimates, exposing a distinction between the model groups.

selected.name: Claims a previously infeasible capability vs incremental benchmark bump
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the abstract claims to make feasible something previously infeasible or unexplored (explicit 'for the first time', 'has remained unexplored', a new capability class). Score 0 if the claim is an incremental accuracy/efficiency improvement on an already-standard, saturated benchmark with no claim of newly-enabled capability.
selected.rationale: R38 states hypergraph curvature 'has remained largely unexplored' and R51 achieves an exact adversarial-accuracy certificate 'for the first time' -- both dense_high_card_low. Contrast R31, which reports an ImageNet accuracy bump 'by up to 5%' on an already-saturated benchmark, and R18, an incremental efficiency-accuracy tradeoff on standard segmentation benchmarks -- both dense_low_card_high.
member_names: Claims a previously infeasible capability vs incremental benchmark bump

selected.name: Improvement stated against prior results rather than prior systems
selected.instruction: Score whether the abstract identifies the specific prior claim it displaces. 10: names prior results (with authors, venue, bound, or exact prior guarantee) and states exactly how this work improves on them, including whether the improvement is near-optimal or matched by a lower bound (improving on a bound with exponential dependence on m+k and on a weaker bi-criteria guarantee; being the first to achieve optimal deployment complexity and optimal dimension dependence simultaneously; naming the exact previous complexity being reduced). 5: prior methods named generically ('previous OOD detection heuristics', 'attention-based NAS') with a qualitative comparison. 0: positioning consists only of 'state-of-the-art' or a benchmark ranking, with no identification of which prior claim is now false or superseded.
selected.rationale: R45 and R57 anchor themselves to specific prior theorems and are near the bottom of the scorecard while mid-to-high for the dense model; R38 does the same with complexities. By contrast R50 and R32 position purely against leaderboards and sit far above their dense rank. Naming the displaced claim is a real quality signal that leaderboard-shaped criteria cannot express.
member_names: Improvement stated against prior results rather than prior systems
Named prior-method engagement together with precise improvement claim

selected.name: Evaluation-to-claim alignment
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the described datasets, tasks, baselines, and evaluation dimensions directly match the stated claims; score 0 when broad claims rest on a narrow or mismatched setup.
selected.rationale: R07 specifies baselines, search spaces, datasets, and tasks matching its HPO claim, while R55 aligns long-term interaction modeling with trajectory datasets.

selected.name: Formalization via Fundamental Mathematical Constructs
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the core contribution is explicitly grounded in mapping the ML problem to a fundamental mathematical domain (e.g., optimal transport, geometry, statistical testing). Score 0 if the method relies on standard ML building blocks (like CNNs or Transformers) without formal mathematical grounding.
selected.rationale: DHL abstracts frequently leverage deep mathematics, such as Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality in R40 or framing OOD detection as statistical hypothesis testing in R41. This elevates the research quality beyond standard empirical tuning, a distinction the dense model captures.
member_names: Cross-Domain Transfer of Deep Mathematical Tools

selected.name: Single dominant insight vs. multi-component aggregation
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the entire contribution is organized around one clear, sharp idea whose significance is immediately graspable and can be stated in a single sentence. Score 0 if the contribution is a combination of multiple known techniques or sub-modules without a unifying insight that makes the whole greater than the parts.
selected.rationale: R06 is organized entirely around one idea: higher-dimensional attention via tensor products of value vectors. R14 centers on one framework: hybrid sequence-graph models for summarization. In contrast, dense-low R04 combines population-size encoding, hypernetworks, and multi-task training without a single insight that unifies them. Dense-low R15 combines hyperbolic networks, self-paced learning, and self-supervision as a multi-component system.
member_names: Single dominant insight vs. multi-component aggregation

selected.name: Native Modeling of Solution Structure
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the formulation explicitly represents multiplicity, counterfactual variation, future interaction, or population dependence as part of the task; score 0 when such structured alternatives are collapsed into a single undifferentiated target.
selected.rationale: R26, R28, R47, and R59 all model alternative labels, valid solutions, future relationships, or population-dependent policies, and mostly belong to the dense-low/card-high group.

selected.name: One decisive result vs scattered multi-benchmark deltas
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the abstract centers on one (or a small number of) decisive, targeted test(s) of the central claim. Score 0 if the abstract lists many small percentage/parameter deltas across many datasets/tasks with no single result standing out as decisive -- a 'kitchen sink' of incremental wins.
selected.rationale: R51 centers on one decisive, exactly-quantified result (first exact adversarial accuracy at a specific epsilon on MNIST) and R39 tests one claim broadly ('little or no loss of accuracy for most tasks') -- both dense_high_card_low. Contrast R49, which lists +1.6% top-1, +0.16M params, +0.07B FLOPs, then separately '3-4% box AP and mask AP', and R19, which lists '6 long-text and 8 short-text datasets from diverse domains' -- both dense_low_card_high.
member_names: One decisive result vs scattered multi-benchmark deltas

selected.name: Contribution isolation
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the abstract distinguishes the role of each component through controlled variants or an explicit diagnosis; score 0 when many additions are bundled with no attribution.
selected.rationale: R14 isolates boundary-focused regularization as protection against degenerate sampling, and R49 identifies the loss formulation as the source of instability.

selected.name: Quantified improvement claims stated with units
selected.instruction: Rate 0-10 the extent to which the abstract states numeric performance figures with explicit units or metric names: percentage accuracy deltas, FID, mIoU, box/mask AP, ROUGE, MAE, nats per image, parameter counts, FLOPs, speed multipliers, 'orders of magnitude'. 0 = no such number anywhere; 5 = one or two figures on a single metric; 10 = many figures spread over several metrics, tasks or datasets. Count occurrences and prominence only. Do NOT assess whether the numbers are large, whether the gains are meaningful, whether the comparison is fair, or whether the measurement was done well.
selected.rationale: Number-dense abstracts are exactly the scorecard's favourites in this slice: R11 (card_pct=0.983 vs dense_pct=0.568; '1.6% Top-1', '0.16M parameters and 0.07B FLOPs', '3-4% box AP and mask AP'), R44 (card_pct=0.885 vs dense_pct=0.094; '10.9% and 12.4% improvement in MAE'), R12 (card_pct=0.774 vs dense_pct=0.158; 'beats the SVM by 6.12%, achieving 96.32%'), R25 (card_pct=0.701; '41.58 nats/image', '66.24 nats/image'). The mirror image is R08 (card_pct=0.359 while dense_pct=0.996) and R58 (card_pct=0.038), which state no figures at all. Whether results are compressed into the abstract as numbers is a writing convention that varies by subfield and era; tagged mixed because having a clean headline number to quote is partly downstream of actually having a result.
member_names: Quantified improvement claims stated with units
selected.upstream_parent: the sub-community's benchmark-table reporting convention and the authors' habit of foregrounding headline figures in the abstract
upstream_parent_all_members: empirical reporting convention and lab writing practice
submission timing and experimental process maturity
the sub-community's benchmark-table reporting convention and the authors' habit of foregrounding headline figures in the abstract

selected.name: Dense inline mathematical notation
selected.instruction: Score the extent to which the abstract contains inline mathematical symbols, Greek letters, or equations. 0 means no mathematical notation, 10 means the text is heavily saturated with equations and symbols. Do not judge the quality or correctness of the math, only the extent of its presence.
selected.rationale: Abstracts with heavy math notation might intimidate a scorecard or signal deep theory to a dense model. R08 and R55 contain dense inline math (e.g., $mathbb{R}^d$, $epsilon$), which affects text-processing perception but is not a direct indicator of overall research quality.

selected.name: Acronym and Method Branding Density
selected.instruction: Rate the extent to which the abstract introduces and repeatedly uses a specific, capitalized acronym or branded name for its proposed method (e.g., 'SNAS', 'PWAN'). 0 means no acronym is used; 10 means the method is heavily branded and repeatedly referenced by its acronym. Do not judge whether the acronym is catchy or good.
selected.rationale: Branding a method with an acronym is a strategic practice that can signal a polished, ready-to-release package to evaluators, biasing scores independently of the core research quality. R14 and R03 both heavily brand and repeat specific acronyms (SNAS, PWAN), a pattern that models might mistakenly read as an indicator of a paper's significance.
upstream_parent_all_members: author's enculturation/fluency in the subfield's insider dialect (practice in the format)

selected.name: Explicit code/model-release disclosure sentence
selected.instruction: Rate 0-10 how explicitly the text announces that code, data, or pretrained models will be or are made publicly available (e.g. a sentence naming a repository or stating that code/models are available). 0 = no such statement; 10 = a prominent, explicit release statement. Do not judge whether release is actually good practice or whether the paper is high quality; score only the presence/prominence of the disclosure sentence.
selected.rationale: R06 ('Code is available at https://github.com/...'), R21 ('we release our code and models at https://github.com/...'), R44 and R49 all carry an explicit release sentence and are all dense_low_card_high, while it is absent from dense_high_card_low items like R05 and R56. A scorecard 'reproducibility' criterion would mechanically reward this sentence regardless of the surrounding science, though labs with a strong open-source habit may also genuinely be more rigorous, hence mixed.
member_names: Evaluation inventory: named datasets, baselines, explicit counts
selected.upstream_parent: author's/lab's practice in the format (open-source engineering culture)
upstream_parent_all_members: author team size / compute-resource access / lab seniority
author's/lab's practice in the format (open-source engineering culture)
the compute budget, GPU access and engineering headcount behind the submission
the producing lab's engineering resources and open-source norms, plus the platform-era convention that artifact links belong in the abstract

selected.name: Promotional claim density
selected.instruction: How much does the abstract use promotional or superlative wording such as “novel,” “first,” “remarkably,” “significant,” “state of the art,” or “outperforms”? Score only wording frequency; do not judge whether the claims are good or true.
selected.rationale: Achievement language can influence reader attention without measuring research merit. Such wording is visible in R03, R17, R46, and R58.

selected.name: Artifact and compliance boilerplate
selected.instruction: How much does the abstract contain code links, pretrained-model announcements, ethics acknowledgments, release statements, or one-sentence-summary boilerplate? Score 0-10 from the text only; do not judge whether the artifacts are useful or the compliance is commendable.
selected.rationale: Required or customary submission language can create recognizable cues unrelated to scientific quality. Examples include the release and compliance material in R03, R21, R53, and R59.

selected.name: Late-riff framing
selected.instruction: How much does the abstract frame its contribution as a revision, alternative, unification, extension, or recombination of several established approaches? Score only this textual framing; do not judge whether the positioning is good, novel, or important.
selected.rationale: An unseen place in a crowded entry stream could encourage direct, late-arriving recombination language, leaving a trace without measuring merit. Such framing appears in R35, R39, R42, and R49.

selected.name: Evidential force of the experiments actually described
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the text states something its experiments established that a reader could not have assumed without them. Judge the substance in context and ignore how much is enumerated. Ask only three things: does the text say what was varied or compared; does it say what specifically happened when it was varied; and does that outcome rule out or narrow some competing account of why the result occurred? Credit concrete checkable statements of direction, magnitude, or condition; ablations or controls that isolate a named cause; comparisons whose held-fixed conditions are stated; negative, mixed, or surprising findings; and explicit statements of what the evidence does not settle. Do NOT reward the surface carrier. Give zero credit for the number of datasets, benchmarks, tasks, languages, domains, model families, model sizes, baselines, seeds, training runs, GPU-hours, annotators, or corpus sizes named, and zero credit for the presence of any scale statement. Brevity, plain wording, small scale, and unfashionable subject matter cost nothing. 10 = each claim made is tied to a specific stated observation, and the text makes clear what would have looked different had the claim been false. 7 = at least one finding is reported precisely enough to check, and the comparison behind it is described. 5 = some concrete outcomes are stated but the central claim rests mainly on assertion. 2 = only that a method was run, applied, or evaluated, plus a bare verdict such as improves or outperforms. 0 = no statement a reader could check appears at all, however many settings are listed. A single experiment on one small dataset, described plainly with no counts and no scale markers, must be able to score 10.
selected.rationale: This isolates the merit the same upstream cause produces: a group able to run many experiments can, if it does good work, learn something discriminating from them. The criterion asks only whether something discriminating is stated, so it is reachable without any resources. Dissociation, high real and low surface: a short abstract on one toy dataset, naming no benchmark counts, no model sizes and no compute, reporting that deleting one component drops accuracy from 0.90 to 0.52 and that the effect disappears once sequences exceed 100 tokens, scores near 10 here and near 0 on the enumeration count. Dissociation, high surface and low real: an abstract naming twelve benchmarks, six languages, four model sizes, thirty baselines and 4,000 GPU-hours whose only reported finding is that the method consistently outperforms prior work scores 10 on the enumeration count and 0 here, because nothing is stated that a reader could check or that could have come out otherwise.
selected.parent: Enumeration count of evaluation settings and resource markers
member_names: Evidential force of the experiments actually described

selected.name: Count of named evaluation settings and resource markers
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 by counting or estimating how many distinct evaluation settings and resource markers the text names, and nothing else. Count each occurrence of: a named or counted dataset or benchmark; a named task; a named language; a named domain; a named model architecture or model family; a model size or parameter count; a transfer, zero-shot, few-shot, fine-tuning, or cross-lingual setting named as a setting; a stated number of baselines or comparison systems; and any explicit scale statement such as compute used, GPU-hours, number of training runs or random seeds, number of human annotators, or corpus size. A count phrase such as twelve benchmarks or six languages counts as that category being present at a large count. 0 = no evaluation setting or resource marker of any kind is named. 2 = exactly one is named. 5 = roughly three or four distinct settings or counts appear. 8 = five to eight appear, or one explicitly large count appears. 10 = many appear, or large counts appear across several of these categories at once. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not decide whether the coverage is adequate, necessary, convincing, redundant, padded, or excessive; do not consider whether anything was learned in those settings; do not consider whether comparisons were controlled or fair; do not consider whether any claim is supported; do not consider whether the writing is clear. If an item lists many settings and reports no finding whatsoever, it must still score 10. Score only the amount of enumeration present on the page.
selected.rationale: This is the pure fingerprint: enumerating settings and resources is what a well-resourced group can do regardless of what it learned, and the judge is forbidden from asking whether the enumeration bought anything. Dissociation, high surface and low real: an abstract listing a dozen benchmarks, several model sizes and a compute budget, ending only with consistent gains, scores 10 here and 0 on the evidential-force component. Dissociation, high real and low surface: a plain abstract with one dataset, no counts and no scale markers that reports exactly what changed under one controlled manipulation and where the effect vanishes scores about 2 here and near 10 there. Because the instruction bars any judgement of adequacy or of what was found, nothing about merit can leak into this score.
selected.parent: Enumeration count of evaluation settings and resource markers
member_names: Count of named evaluation settings and resource markers
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Enumeration count of evaluation settings and resource markers

selected.name: Scope earned by reported variation across genuinely different regimes
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the text earns the scope of its own claim by reporting how behaviour differed across conditions that plainly differ in kind. Judge substance in context. Ask: are the conditions the claim rests on actually different from one another in a way the text identifies, for example a different data regime, language family, domain, distribution shift, scale, or deployment condition, rather than interchangeable variants of one thing? And does the text report how the result changed, held, or broke across them, including where it stops holding? Credit stated boundary conditions, per-condition or disaggregated outcomes, transfer that is described rather than merely asserted, explicit statements of the population or setting the claim is meant to cover, and a stated scope that matches the conditions described rather than exceeding them. Do NOT reward the surface carrier. Give zero credit for the number of datasets, benchmarks, tasks, languages, domains, architectures, model sizes, baselines, or settings listed, zero credit for count phrases such as twelve benchmarks or six languages, and zero credit for breadth-signalling wording such as extensive, comprehensive, thorough, wide range, diverse, large-scale, multilingual, cross-domain, cross-lingual, in-the-wild, or at scale. Words asserting breadth are worth nothing here; only reported behaviour across identified differences counts. Two conditions handled honestly outrank twenty undifferentiated ones. 10 = the text names conditions that differ in kind, says what changed between them, and states where the claim ceases to hold. 6 = two or more genuinely different conditions are named and only aggregate behaviour is reported. 3 = differing conditions are named but nothing is said about how anything differed. 0 = scope is asserted or listed only, or every condition named is a variant of the same regime, so no generality is demonstrated.
selected.rationale: The same upstream cause that lets a group list wide coverage can also let it establish genuinely general findings; this component keeps the generality and drops the listing. It is reachable by a short unfashionable item because two well-chosen contrasting conditions suffice, and unreachable by vocabulary because breadth words are explicitly worth zero. Dissociation, high real and low surface: a brief abstract that tests exactly two conditions, high-resource English and a low-resource morphologically rich language, reports that the method holds in the first and degrades past a stated data threshold in the second, and uses no breadth vocabulary at all, scores near 10 here and about 3 on the extent count. Dissociation, high surface and low real: an abstract stacking extensive experiments, comprehensive evaluation across diverse domains and large-scale multilingual, and listing fourteen datasets that are all English news classification, with only an aggregate claim of consistent gains, scores 10 on the extent count and 0 here, because no condition differs in kind and no difference across conditions is reported.
selected.parent: Extent of coverage listing and breadth vocabulary
member_names: Scope earned by reported variation across genuinely different regimes

selected.name: Extent of coverage listing and breadth-signalling phrasing
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 by counting or estimating two things together and nothing else. First, the number of coverage items listed: datasets, benchmarks, tasks, domains, languages, model architectures, model sizes, baselines, or experimental settings, whether named individually or given as a count such as twelve benchmarks or six languages. Second, the number of occurrences of breadth-signalling phrasing, such as extensive experiments, comprehensive evaluation, a wide range of, across diverse, large-scale, multilingual, cross-domain, cross-lingual, zero-shot, in-the-wild, at scale, exhaustive, or thorough ablations. 0 = no coverage items are listed and no such phrasing appears. 3 = one or two listed items, or a single breadth phrase. 6 = several listed items, or one breadth phrase plus a short list. 8 = a long list in one category, or two or three breadth phrases. 10 = a long enumeration spanning multiple categories, or several breadth phrases stacked together, or both. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not decide whether the listed coverage is adequate, appropriate, persuasive, redundant, or padded; do not consider whether the conditions differ from one another in any meaningful way; do not consider whether any result across them is reported; do not consider whether the breadth vocabulary is warranted or empty. An item that lists a dozen benchmarks and reports only that it consistently outperforms must still score 10.
selected.rationale: This is the carrier alone: quantity of listing plus breadth diction, with every question about warrant stripped out, so it can be maximised by writing style and access to compute without any demonstrated generality. Dissociation, high surface and low real: fourteen interchangeable English datasets plus three breadth phrases and only an aggregate verdict scores 10 here and 0 on the earned-scope component. Dissociation, high real and low surface: a two-condition study reporting exactly where the effect degrades, written with no breadth words, scores about 3 here and near 10 there. The explicit bar on judging whether conditions differ meaningfully is what keeps genuine generality out of this score.
selected.parent: Extent of coverage listing and breadth vocabulary
member_names: Extent of coverage listing and breadth-signalling phrasing
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Extent of coverage listing and breadth vocabulary

selected.name: Precision and checkability of the stated claim, notation aside
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how precisely and checkably the text states what it claims, judged on substance and in whatever language the text happens to use. Ask: is it clear exactly what object, setting, or population the claim is about; what conditions it requires; what it asserts; and what it excludes? Credit stated assumptions and where they bind; quantified statements saying how much, in what units, in what regime, or relative to what alternative; explicit separation of what is proved from what is observed, approximated, or conjectured; named failure modes or regimes where the claim does not hold; and definitions supplied for any term or symbol the claim depends on. Plain prose counts exactly as much as symbols: a sentence saying that error falls roughly with the square root of the sample size provided the noise has bounded variance, and that this fails once samples are correlated, is as precise as the same content in notation, and must be able to score 10. Do NOT reward the surface carrier. Give zero credit for the presence, quantity, density, or apparent difficulty of formal vocabulary or notation: no credit for the words theorem, lemma, proposition, proof, bound, convergence, rate, minimax, complexity, estimator, optimality, or guarantee as such, and no credit for Greek letters, single-letter variables, subscripts, superscripts, norms, expectations, big-O or Omega expressions, inequalities, operator symbols, or displayed formulas as such. Symbols used without definition and results asserted without their conditions count against precision, not for it. 10 = the claim, the conditions under which it is asserted, and its limits are stated exactly enough that a reader could say what observation or counterexample would contradict it. 7 = the claim and its main condition are exact, but its magnitude or its limits are left open. 4 = the claim is intelligible but its conditions and magnitude are vague. 0 = a reader cannot tell what is being asserted or under what conditions, however formal or technical the wording appears.
selected.rationale: The same upstream cause behind heavy formalism, namely working in a theory-adjacent tradition with the training to be exact, also produces genuinely exact claims; this component keeps the exactness and discards the typography. It is reachable by plain unfashionable prose because natural-language statements of conditions and magnitudes count fully, and unreachable by symbol density because undefined notation is explicitly penalised. Dissociation, high real and low surface: a symbol-free abstract stating that a simple counting rule recovers the correct answer whenever fewer than a third of the inputs are corrupted, that it fails above that fraction, and that the guarantee assumes independent corruptions, scores near 10 here and about 2 on the density count. Dissociation, high surface and low real: an abstract dense with theorem, minimax-optimal, convergence rate, Greek letters, norms and big-O expressions, none of the symbols defined and no assumption or regime stated, so no reader could say what it rules out, scores 10 on the density count and 0 here.
selected.parent: Density of formal vocabulary and mathematical notation on the page
member_names: Precision and checkability of the stated claim, notation aside

selected.name: Density of formal vocabulary and mathematical notation
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the raw extent of formal-mathematical vocabulary and notation in the text, counting or estimating only. Count occurrences of formal-mathematical vocabulary such as theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, proof, bound, convergence, rate, assumption, regularity, convexity, smoothness, optimality, minimax, complexity, estimator, guarantee, and close relatives; and any inline notation such as Greek letters, single-letter variable names, subscripts or superscripts, norms, expectations, probability symbols, big-O or Omega expressions, inequalities, set or operator symbols, and displayed formulas. 0 = none of these markers appears anywhere. 3 = one or two isolated markers in the whole text. 5 = markers appear in a few places but most sentences have none. 7 = markers recur across several sentences. 10 = such vocabulary and notation are dense from the first sentence to the last. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not consider whether the formalism is correct, rigorous, necessary, well used, or informative; do not consider whether anything is actually proved; do not consider whether symbols are defined or whether assumptions are stated; do not consider whether the prose is clear or the claim intelligible. An item saturated with symbols that states nothing a reader could check must still score 10, and a fully precise item written entirely in plain words must score near 0.
selected.rationale: This is the fingerprint with all merit removed: it measures typography and diction only, and the judge is barred from asking whether the formalism is defined, correct, or load-bearing, so it can be maximised by an item with no checkable content. Dissociation, high surface and low real: an abstract packed with undefined Greek letters, norms, big-O expressions and the word minimax, stating no assumption and no regime, scores 10 here and 0 on the precision component. Dissociation, high real and low surface: a plain-prose abstract stating the exact corruption fraction under which its rule provably works and the independence assumption it needs scores about 2 here and near 10 there.
selected.parent: Density of formal vocabulary and mathematical notation on the page
member_names: Density of formal vocabulary and mathematical notation
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Density of formal vocabulary and mathematical notation on the page
